origin.description: Adds an empirical Lorenz curve to an existing plot.

arguments.name: general
arguments.text: If TRUE, add the generalized Lorenz curve instead of the ordinary one.

arguments.name: lwd, ...
arguments.text: Line width and further arguments passed to lines, including col.

origin.details: This is the curve drawn by plot.Lc without the diagonal. It is meant to be called after a plot is already open, for example to compare two provinces or the lower and upper grouped curves.

translation.description: Adds an empirical Lorenz curve to the current axes.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A dict with NumPy arrays p, L, and L.general, as returned by Lc.

arguments.name: general
arguments.text: If true, add L.general instead of L.

arguments.name: lwd
arguments.text: Line width. A linewidth entry in style replaces it.

arguments.name: ax
arguments.text: Axes to draw on. None uses the current axes.

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: Extra Matplotlib line options, such as color. The default color is black.

translation.details: Only the curve is added. The diagonal is left to plot_lc. Pass color to match a second series drawn with R's col.
translation.value: A dict with the plotted coordinates, p and y.
translation.example:
from ineq.lorenz import Lc
from ineq.plots import lines_lc, plot_lc

x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
n = [482, 825, 722, 690, 661, 760, 745, 2140, 1911, 1024]
plot_lc(Lc(x, n=n))
lines_lc(Lc(x), color="C1")
